## Why This Is Asked

Tests the ability to pack multiple fields into a single word, a common task in serialization and network protocols. It emphasizes precise bit-width handling and avoiding branches.

## Key Concepts

- Bitwise masking
- Bit shifts
- Field packing into a 32-bit word

## Code Example

```javascript
function packHeader(version, flags, length) {
  return ((version & 0x0F) << 28) | ((flags & 0xFF) << 20) | (length & 0xFFFFF);
}
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you extract version, flags, and length from the header?
- How would you validate inputs to prevent overflow or sign issues in languages with signed integers?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests knowledge of bitwise rotations, a common low-level operation, and handling edge cases when k wraps around 32 without using branches. It also demonstrates how to make shifts robust against k=0 or k=31.

## Key Concepts
- Bitwise rotation using shifts and OR
- Modulo wrapping using masking and two's complement tricks
- Avoiding undefined shifts for k=0

## Code Example
```javascript
function rotateLeft32(n, k) {
  k = k & 31;
  return ((n << k) | (n >>> ((-k) & 31))) >>> 0;
}
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to implement a rotation primitive with wrap-around using only shifts and masks, including masking to handle large r and the n=0 edge case.

## Key Concepts
- Circular shift using (x << n) | (x >> (32 - n))
- Masking r with 31 to confine to 0..31
- Edge-case n=0 preserves x exactly

## Code Example
```c
static inline uint32_t rotl32(uint32_t x, unsigned r) {
  unsigned n = r & 31; // 0..31
  return (x << n) | (x >> (32 - n));
}
```
